concept: Unique, TTL and shard-key indexes that read as unused
summary: Source-anchored research for Unique, TTL and shard-key indexes that read as unused. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A unique index can enforce uniqueness while accesses.ops remains zero: checking uniqueness during INSERT does not increment this counter. Removing an index solely because of zero accesses can remove a required integrity constraint. (high confidence)

$indexStats accesses.ops measures index access driven by user requests; it excludes internal TTL deletion and chunk split or migration activity. A zero counter therefore cannot establish that an index has no operational purpose. (high confidence)

Hiding preserves uniqueness enforcement, TTL expiration, and index maintenance. Inference: a successful hidden-index trial tests query dependence but cannot establish that removing a unique or TTL index preserves application semantics. (high confidence)

For ordinary shard-key index protection, the supporting index may be the shard-key index itself or a compound index with the shard key as its prefix. MongoDB documents that the only non-hidden supporting index cannot be hidden or dropped; the hashed-key exception requires separate handling. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The blanket assertion that every shard-key index must always remain is too broad. MongoDB introduced dropping hashed shard-key indexes in 7.0.3, 6.0.12 and 5.0.22; its documented procedure warns that balancing for the collection stops and orphan cleanup cannot proceed without that index. It recommends a supporting non-hashed index and checking for orphans before removal. (high confidence)

An audit must preserve index properties alongside usage counts. The My DBA World script projects only name, since, and accesses, while $indexStats supplies a full spec. Inference: that script output alone cannot identify unique or TTL constraints. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mydbaworld.com/indexes-usage-all-collections-all-databases-mongodb/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats.md

On ranged sharded collections, unique indexes generally require the shard key as a prefix, with the default _id index as an exception. If _id is not the shard key, its index enforces uniqueness per shard rather than across the cluster; index review must preserve the actual constraint scope. (high confidence)

An automated audit should inspect the index specification before acting on zero accesses. The full spec is included in $indexStats, and TTL indexes are created with the expireAfterSeconds option, whose valid range includes 0, so detect TTL by the presence of expireAfterSeconds rather than a truthiness check. Excluding unique and shard-key-supporting indexes is a conservative policy used by the mdbkit tool. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl.md ; https://github.com/saqibameen86/mdbkit

A TTL index may expire documents while its recorded accesses remain zero. Treat expireAfterSeconds as evidence of a retention function that must be reviewed separately from query usage. (high confidence)

A historical MongoDB production incident on 4.4.18 involved dropping a shard-key index on one shard, followed by queued deletion tasks and degraded performance. The ticket reports rebuilding the index and scaling up to let deletions catch up; it does not establish that an unused-index tool caused the drop. (low confidence)

The mdbkit author excludes unique, TTL, hidden and shard-key-supporting indexes from unused-index candidates, noting that the TTL monitor's deletes do not count as index use. This is one tool author's conservative classification, not an independent proof of MongoDB semantics. Sources: https://github.com/saqibameen86/mdbkit

The blanket rule that shard-key indexes can never be dropped is too broad: MongoDB permits dropping hashed shard-key indexes starting in 7.0.3, 6.0.12, and 5.0.22. This exception requires a separate operational review. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The hashed-index drop procedure warns that removal disables balancing for that collection and prevents remaining orphan cleanup. It recommends a supporting non-hashed index to avoid shard-key-filter collection scans; recreate the hashed index to restore balancing eligibility. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Treat zero-access indexes as review candidates: inspect unique and TTL properties in the index spec returned by $indexStats, and confirm that no semantic change results before removal. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats.md
